page.overview:
Who is Henry Loomis?

Dr. Henry Loomis is a paleontologist and principal character in . The character, per director Gareth Edwards, is "very comfortable on digs and expeditions but not the life-and-death risks" and is “out of his depth in terms of the military element of the mission".

Prior to 2027, Dr. Loomis conducted his postdoctoral research under the supervision of Dr. Alan Grant.

By 2027, Dr. Loomis worked at a museum in New York that was closing due to a loss of public interest in dinosaurs, which were dying off because the modern climate of Earth was becoming inhospitable to them. For the past six months, Dr. Loomis had been advising Parker-Genix on paleo-coronary health for developing a drug that could cure heart disease with the DNA of three selected dinosaurs. Zora Bennett and Martin Krebs, the representative of Parker-Genix, summoned Dr. Loomis to join a team to collect blood samples from the selected creatures - Titanosaurus, Mosasaurus and Quetzalcoatlus - on Ile Saint-Hubert. This island is located near French Guiana in the equatorial region, where the climate is suitable for dinosaurs.

While tracking the Mosasaurus to collect its DNA sample, Dr. Loomis observed the Spinosaurus and the Mosasaurus hunting together, displaying mutualism. When he saw the Titanosaurus, he got close to the legs of one of them and touched it. He had never seen a dinosaur in its natural habitat before, only in a theme park or wandering around cities.
